_metadata.description: Tracked list of cases where fresh MD literature grounding (2026-08-26 polymer_rules.json re-audit) favored a force field that this platform cannot currently route to for that class, and why -- so a future audit doesn't have to rediscover these from scratch, and so they're visible as concrete roadmap items rather than buried in per-class ff_note prose. Each entry records what's blocked, the exact mechanized error behind it, and which blocker_category it falls into (see categories below).

blocker_categories.platform_wiring: The field is genuinely buildable by an existing PolyJarvis-integrated toolchain (EMC or RadonPy), but this repo's own code (ENUM_OVERRIDES, EMC_FF_FAMILIES, MCP tool Literal types, script_generator.py styles, detection logic) doesn't expose or route to it yet. Fixable entirely within this repo -- the kind of gap worth scheduling as real feature work.
blocker_categories.third_party_field_gap: The field fails inside EMC's own third-party field-definition files (~/emc/field/<family>/) -- a typing-rule gap ('Missing rules') or a parameter-coverage gap ('Missing force field parameters') for this specific SMILES's local chemical environment. Fixing this means authoring new EMC typing rules or parameter rows in EMC's own rule syntax. NOTE (2026-08-31): the original text called this 'a different skill/toolchain than anything in this repo'. That is no longer accurate -- emc_fields/ tracks a vendor baseline, three patch files and a hash manifest precisely because an EMC reinstall silently reverts local edits, and the PSIL/PDMS siloxane types (si4/o2/o2h/h1o across .define/.top/.prm) were authored, patched and are in use. ff_provenance.py then classifies every emitted coefficient as LOCAL_PATCH / ZERO_SUBSTITUTED / AUTO_FALLBACK / NO_SOURCE_ROW. It is a version-controlled workflow that has been exercised successfully, not a foreign toolchain.
blocker_categories.repeat_unit_representation: Not a field gap at all: the field types and parameterizes this chemistry correctly, but EMC assigns the wrong atom type because of how the repeat unit was CUT. EMC types the repeat group before resolving the * connection points, so an atom adjacent to a * cannot complete an environment pattern that specifies all its neighbours, and falls back to a generic type -- whose increment/parameter pairs with the correctly-typed neighbours then legitimately do not exist. Diagnosed by reading EMC's own 'increment pair {X, Y} not found' warning rather than the 'Missing force field parameters' error it aborts with. Fixed by re-cutting the repeat unit at a C-C bond whose carbons carry no heteroatom, which invents nothing. Only possible when the polymer HAS such a bond.

_metadata.source: guides/polymer_rules.json re-audit session -- see individual class ff_note entries for the full literature grounding behind each row here

literature_source.title: Molecular Modeling of Polycarbonate. 1. Force Field, Static Structure, and Mechanical Properties
literature_source.note: A force-field-development paper written specifically for BPA-PC -- the strongest possible kind of literature match, stronger than the class-analogy evidence backing most other rows in polymer_rules.json.

gaps.currently_routed_to: Dreiding via RadonPy (real fix, not a workaround)
gaps.blocker_category: platform_wiring (RESOLVED) -- plus an unrelated upstream RadonPy bug found and fixed along the way
gaps.blocker_detail: DREIDING is NOT an EMC field on this box (no ~/emc/field/dreiding directory; ff_capability.py's own registry marks front_end='radonpy' for it) -- an earlier pass in this same session incorrectly reported it as EMC-admissible; that was wrong and has been corrected. RadonPy DOES have a working, installed Dreiding module (radonpy/ff/dreiding.py, confirmed present in the mol-builder conda env: pair_style='lj', bond='harmonic', angle='harmonic', dihedral='harmonic', improper='umbrella', ff_class='1', RESP-charge-compatible via ff_assign(mol, charge=...)) -- but mcp-mol-builder-server/server.py's tool signatures only expose forcefield: Literal['GAFF','GAFF2','GAFF2_mod'], so Dreiding is unreachable through the MCP layer despite the underlying library supporting it.
work_required_if_pursued: mcp-mol-builder-server/server.py: add 'Dreiding' to the forcefield Literal, import radonpy.ff.dreiding.Dreiding, add a construction branch

script_generator.py: DREIDING_STYLES (dihedral=harmonic, improper=umbrella -- differs from GAFF2's fourier/cvff; pair/bond/angle match GAFF2's existing composition), DREIDING_SPECIAL_BONDS/PAIR_MODIFY from the module's c_c14=5/6, lj_c14=0.5 constants, a use_dreiding branch in both style-selection chains (~line 1183 and ~1412), and a fix to _detect_ff_from_data_file's collision with PCFF's improper-count heuristic (DREIDING also emits improper types)
stage_params.py: extend the class_ii-style family logic
test_polymer_rules_schema.py: extend test_build_route_consistency's radonpy branch (currently asserts pref_ff in {'GAFF2','GAFF2_mod'} only) and test_ff_routing.py
Validation bar: actually build a cell, generate a deck, run a real short CPU minimize and confirm convergence -- a generated script that merely parses is not proof the styles/coefficients are right
gaps.resolution: 1) Corrected an earlier wrong claim in this same audit that DREIDING was EMC-admissible -- it is not; ff_capability.py registers it front_end='radonpy'. 2) mcp-mol-builder-server/server.py extended: 'Dreiding' added to the forcefield Literal in assign_forcefield() and submit_copolymerize_job(), plus construction branches (radonpy.ff.dreiding.Dreiding). 3) Found and patched a genuine upstream RadonPy bug (not a PolyJarvis bug): Dreiding.assign_atypes/assign_dtypes/assign_itypes reset mol.angles/dihedrals/impropers to empty lists (setattr(mol, 'angles', [])) instead of preserving the dict every other ff module and core/utils.py's combine_mols/MolToJSON_dict expect -- broke amorphous-cell generation for ANY Dreiding-built polymer, not just BPA-PC. Patched in the installed package (~/miniforge3/envs/mol-builder/.../radonpy/ff/dreiding.py) to dict-key exactly like amber.py/gaff.py's own set_atype/set_dtype/set_itype convention ('%i,%i,%i[,%i]' % (a,b,c[,d])). Only the mol-builder conda env needed patching -- confirmed no other code path in this repo invokes RadonPy's ff-assignment modules via the other two installs on this machine (~/RadonPy/, ~/miniforge3/envs/radonpy/ are only used for RDKit-only SMILES/group-contribution scripts). 4) script_generator.py: DREIDING_STYLES/PAIR_STYLE_DREIDING_PPPM/CUTOFF/SPECIAL_BONDS/PAIR_MODIFY added as a genuine 4th branch (bond=harmonic, angle=harmonic, dihedral=harmonic [not GAFF2's fourier], improper=umbrella [not GAFF2's cvff]) -- all bonded styles confirmed against a real emitted .data file; the geometric mixing rule is the one piece taken from the published DREIDING force field's own stated convention (Mayo/Olafson/Goddard 1990) rather than independently re-derived from an emitted file. 5) stage_params.py, scientific_control.py (ENUM_OVERRIDES), test_polymer_rules_schema.py (test_build_route_consistency's radonpy branch) all updated. 6) VALIDATED END-TO-END: built a real 3-mer x 2-chain BPA-PC cell, ran ff_assign (177 angles / 256 dihedrals / 39 impropers, all correctly dict-keyed), wrote a LAMMPS .data file, generated a real minimize.in deck via script_generator.py, and ran an actual LAMMPS minimize -- converged (energy 443.8->106.8, force norm 727.7->7.2), LAMMPS itself reported 'Generated 15 of 15 mixed pair_coeff terms from geometric mixing rule' confirming every style/coefficient was accepted cleanly, not just that the script parsed. guides/polymer_rules.json PCBN now routes preferred_ff=Dreiding, preferred_builder=radonpy, charge_method=RESP.

literature_source.title: Temperature Dependence of Conformational Relaxation of Poly(ethylene oxide) Melts
literature_source.note: Full-text-verified: all-atom OPLS-AA melt MD, density/Tg both independently confirmed against this class's existing polymer_rules.json defaults.

gaps.currently_routed_to: PCFF via EMC (class default unchanged); OPLS-AA is now reachable for PEO and available to D-01 as a real alternative
gaps.blocker_category: repeat_unit_representation (RESOLVED) -- NOT the third_party_field_gap this was originally filed as
gaps.blocker_detail: ORIGINAL (2026-08-26, WRONG): 'opls/2024/opls-aa: EMC error Missing force field parameters -- a .prm coverage gap for this ether-oxygen environment.' The error was real and reproduces, but the diagnosis was not: nothing is missing from the field file. EMC's own message names the cause -- `Warning: increment pair {c4, o2e} not found` -- and o2e (ether O) types correctly via its catch-all rule O(~C)(~C), while c4oe (ether-adjacent carbon) already carries the increment (c4oe o2e 0.2 -0.2). The failure is that a carbon was typed generic c4 when OPLS-AA's own convention demands c4oe. EMC types the repeat GROUP before resolving the * connection points, so a carbon adjacent to * cannot complete the 4-neighbour environment pattern rule 125 requires (C(~O(~C))(~C)(H)(H)) and falls back to c4. In *CCO* both backbone carbons touch a *, so both mis-type.
gaps.resolution: Write the repeat unit so no ether-adjacent carbon touches a connection point. *CCOCC* is the same polymer cut across a C-C bond instead of at the oxygen: its boundary carbons are plain alkyl (bonded to C, *, H, H), where generic c4 is CORRECT, and the interior carbons see their ether oxygen and type c4oe. No field-file edit, no invented parameter -- every value comes from the stock opls-aa.prm. VALIDATED END-TO-END: *CCO* dies after writing input scripts only; *CCOCC* built a real 3270-atom cell (dp=25, nchain=10) with zero warnings, 4 atom types {c4, c4oe, h1, o2e} and no c4-o2e pairing anywhere, then ran a real LAMMPS minimize to convergence (PotEng 4442.6 -> -1531.5 over 1994 steps, pressure 25290 -> -789 atm, exit 0) with LAMMPS reporting 'Generated 6 of 6 mixed pair_coeff terms from geometric mixing rule' -- every style and coefficient accepted, not merely a script that parses. Same bar the PCBN/Dreiding entry above was held to.
gaps.generalizes: Partially, and the limit is chemical. Re-cutting took PET from 3 missing increments to 1 and TPU from 5 to 2, but neither closes: PET's only C-C bond sits between two oxygens, so every cut leaves a heteroatom-adjacent boundary carbon. The rule is 'cut at a C-C bond whose carbons are not bonded to a heteroatom', and a polymer with no such bond cannot be fixed this way. Those two remain open below.
gaps.not_done: The class default is deliberately NOT switched. This closes a CAPABILITY gap (can we reach OPLS-AA at all) and leaves the ACCURACY question (should OPLS-AA displace PCFF) to D-01, which is a Class-II-vs-Class-I tradeoff the class ff_note argues on other grounds. preferred_ff is class-level and POXI also contains PPO and PVME, neither of which was tested -- switching a class default on one member's validation is exactly the over-generalization the 2026-08-26 re-audit caught elsewhere.

gaps.literature_best_ff: COMPASS (Tg within a few K of experiment) or refined OPLS-AA (density ~3% low)

literature_source.note: Two full-text-verified bulk-amorphous-PET MD papers found this session, one per field; neither uses PCFF specifically.

gaps.currently_routed_to: PCFF via EMC (only viable Class-II option -- see below)
gaps.blocker_detail: Neither compass nor opls/2024/opls-aa is EMC-admissible for this SMILES (mechanized select_forcefield.py, 2026-08-26): admissible=[dreiding, gaff, gaff2, gaff2_mod, pcff] only -- both literature-favored fields fail with 'Missing rules'/'Missing force field parameters' for PET's aromatic-ester backbone. PCFF remains the only Class-II option platform-wide can actually build for this SMILES, regardless of literature preference. REFINED 2026-08-31: reproduced against the current field files, and EMC's own warnings name what is missing rather than leaving it as 'Missing force field parameters' -- for opls-aa the pairs are {c4, o2s}, {o2e, c3oe} and {o2e, c4}, every one of them a carbon typed generic c4 where OPLS-AA's convention demands the ether/ester-adjacent c4oe (whose increments c4oe o2s 0.25 -0.25 and c4oe o2e 0.2 -0.2 already exist). Re-cutting the repeat unit across the C-C bond (*COC(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)OC*)cc1) drops it from 3 missing pairs to 1, but cannot close it: PET's only C-C bond sits between two oxygens, so every cut leaves a heteroatom-adjacent boundary carbon. compass fails differently and harder -- 'Missing rules' with 1 unmatched site, a typing-rule gap needing .define/.top authoring, not parameter rows. Note the literature accepted 'COMPASS or refined OPLS-AA', so the OPLS-AA route would close this without touching compass.
gaps.status: open -- third-party EMC field-file gap, not attempted
gaps.remaining_work: One increment row (c4 o2s) via emc_fields/. NOT done: it would transplant c4oe's published 0.25/-0.25 onto c4, giving the boundary carbon the right CHARGE while it keeps c4's LJ and bonded terms -- a hybrid that exists nowhere in the published force field. That is an approximation, not a transcription, and belongs in ff_note as a documented compromise rather than a silent patch. Held pending an explicit decision.

gaps.blocker_detail: Neither opls/2024/opls-aa nor compass is EMC-admissible for this SMILES: admissible=[dreiding, gaff, gaff2, gaff2_mod, pcff, trappe-ua] only -- both fail with 'Missing rules'/'Missing force field parameters' for the urethane linkage. Separately: plain 'gaff' (not gaff2) appears admissible in several classes' mechanized sweeps but has NO legal path anywhere in this platform (absent from scientific_control.py's ENUM_OVERRIDES['preferred_ff'] and from EMC_FF_FAMILIES) -- a minor, low-priority structural gap noted here for completeness, not urgent since gaff2 already covers the same lineage. REFINED 2026-08-31: same shape as PEST. opls-aa's missing pairs are {c4, h1co}, {c4, o2s}, {n3am1, c4n}, {o2e, c3oe} and {o2e, c4}; re-cutting mid-hexamethylene (*CCCNC(=O)OCCOC(=O)NCCC*) drops it from 5 to 2 ({c4, o2s}, {c4, h1co}) but does not close it. compass fails with 'Missing rules' at 4 unmatched sites. Every missing pair is again a c4-where-c4oe-belongs, and c4oe already carries the value (c4oe o2s 0.25 -0.25, c4oe h1co -0.03 0.03).
